note:
Ran natively on ordinary Windows (no WSL2; none installed), Python 3.12.10, AMD64, at commit c24b47ce9f159b2424ed800f9ebbc41eb1795c5e cloned from github.com/Raoof128/Project-Simurgh with full history. The folder I received contained only the three handoff files and two cover notes; every evidence pack came from the cloned repository. The repository's copy of HANDOFF.md is byte-identical to the folder's copy. Findings, in the order they bit:
1) 17 phases (19a, 19c, 19e, 19h, 19i, 19j, 19k, 19l, 19m, 19n, 19o, 19p, 19q, 19r, 19t, 19u, 19v) refused with ValueError('protocol_inventory') before printing any receipt. Cause: evidence.py expected_sources() builds the source set with pathlib, which on Windows yields backslash separators (e.g. 'tools\assurance-provenance\projection.py'), while the committed protocol.json 'sources' keys use forward slashes, so set(p['sources']) != expected_sources() on every native-Windows run. I confirmed this read-only, by printing expected_sources() next to the protocol.json keys; the two sets differ only in separator.
2) 19s refused earlier, with ValueError('prompt_binding'): monitor19s.prompt() pins docs/research/provenance-phase-19s/third-party/sleight-bench/control_arena.md by sha256, and this clone checked it out with CRLF endings (git core.autocrlf=true on this machine; the repository ships no .gitattributes), so the digest no longer matches PROMPT_SHA256.
3) 19b and 19g refused earlier than HANDOFF.md predicts. Not with "No module named 'openai'" but with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl' (tools/assurance-composed-successor/successor.py line 21). fcntl does not exist on Windows. The hash-locked verify set itself installs cleanly on Windows (pip --require-hashes --only-binary exits 0; every wheel resolves for win_amd64), but the same fcntl failure repeats with the verify-set interpreter, so the openai failure the document expects is never reached on Windows.
4) 19d refused with RuntimeError('host_cannot_namespace'), the refusal HANDOFF.md anticipates for hosts without user/network namespaces.
5) handoff19.py check could not compare anything: no phase produced a receipt JSON, so the comparator raised json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) for each phase; that line is recorded verbatim per phase under 'discrepancies'.
6) Not run on this host: --replay on 19a/19j/19l/19p/19t (Linux x86_64 only; this machine has WSL2 installed but no Linux distribution, and the operator chose not to install Ubuntu), the 19b Lean differential (Lean 4.15.0 absent), and the 19d namespace probe (recorded as the host_cannot_namespace refusal above).
7) The test suite (cd tools/assurance-provenance && python -m unittest discover -s tests -v) was run with the verify-set interpreter; see the tests outcome below the phases in this note.
No file in the repository was edited; the only additions are the two virtual environments the HANDOFF.md recipes themselves prescribe (.venv-verify) and Python bytecode is suppressed with -B.
8) Test suite outcome: exit=1. unittest summary line: "Ran 652 tests in 688.915s" / "FAILED (failures=19, errors=50, skipped=22)" (verbose stderr; 11.5 min of test time, 12.1 min stage time on this laptop).
Causes seen in the trace: 10 occurrences of "No module named 'fcntl'" (module import failures via the frozen successor chain: test_approval, test_drill19, test_evidence19b, test_evidence19g and others); 28 mentions of protocol_inventory and 6 of prompt_binding (the same two Windows causes as the verifier refusals above); and 4 errors in test_egress19 raising "AttributeError: module 'socket' has no attribute 'AF_UNIX'" - HANDOFF.md says the namespace tests "skip, not pass, where their host requirement is unmet", but on Windows they error instead of skipping. No occurrence of "No module named 'openai'" anywhere in the run.
